newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha unmoved, Feb LSWR trade mostly done.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha unmoved, Feb LSWR trade mostly done.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were virtually unchanged in Monday afternoon trade amid a lack of fresh incentives, traders said.
Backwardation in naphtha"s inter-month spreads remained wide, with first-half April/first-half May indicated at plus $8.00/10.00.
Second-half April open-spec naphtha was quoted at $233.00/235.00 per tonne, little changed from Friday"s levels.
First-half May was assessed at $230.00/231.00. On Friday, it was sold from a European major to a Japanese trader at $230.00. Also on Friday, first-half April was sold at $239.50.
Trading for February lifting Indonesian low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) was almost over, with few keen sellers left in the market, traders said.
About 1.6 million barrels of February lots were destined for South Korea and 1.4 million for Japan, they said.
South Korea"s LSWR demand is expected to slow down towards the spring as electric utilities are expected to burn more natural gas at their power plants, traders said.
In winter, power firms tend to depend less on natural gas and more on LSWR for power generation as household demand for natural gas grows, they said.--Tokyo Energy Desk
